paper1.title: Scalable and consistent few-shot classification of survey responses using text embeddings
paper1.description: We introduce a text embedding-based classification framework for efficient qualitative analysis of open-ended survey responses. Requiring only a handful of examples, this method integrates seamlessly into existing workflows and achieves performance comparable to expert human coders. It enables scalable, consistent, and audit-friendly analysis of thousands of responses.

paper2.title: Using Text Embeddings for Qualitative Analysis at Scale
paper2.description: We propose a novel technique for deductive qualitative data analysis using text embeddings. By representing text in a high-dimensional meaning space, we can quantify differences and model topics more flexibly than traditional methods. Validate against established datasets, our approach recovers key trends and offers a scalable solution for large text corpora.

paper3.title: DANTE: Deductive Content Analysis Using Text Embeddings
paper3.description: Traditional qualitative content analysis of text is labor-intensive. We introduce DANTE, a reliable and transparent few-shot tool that makes text embedding-based qualitative analysis more accessible. It enables researchers to perform large-scale deductive content analysis without extensive programming skills.

In his spare time, he plays Norwegian folk fiddle, carves wood, and reads graphic novels.

PCompare.intro: Legal research happens under pressure, and there is no room for mistakes. Generative tools produce text, and occasionally produce citations that do not exist. Presedens builds a representation of the meaning of your question and retrieves matching paragraphs from real legal sources. Every result is a document you can open and verify.
PCompare.genericVerdict: The cited decision does not exist, and even when a source is real, it is buried in analysis you never asked for.
PCompare.presedensAnswerSuffix: each opening to the authoritative text, with the matching paragraphs highlighted.
PCompare.presedensVerdict: Retrieved, not generated. The source is the answer.

PCaps.heading: Built for how procurement lawyers actually work.
PCaps.c1Body: Ask in plain legal language. Presedens finds decisions that answer your question even when they use entirely different wording: no boolean syntax, no guessing the tribunal’s vocabulary.
PCaps.c2Body: Hits point to the specific paragraph in a decision, not just the document. You land on the reasoning that matters, not page one of forty.
PCaps.c3Body: Open a decision or statute and the matching paragraphs are highlighted in place, so you see at a glance which parts of the document are relevant.
PCaps.c4Body: Narrow by decision type, outcome, section of the decision, date and parties, each filter showing how many results it returns.
PCaps.c6Body: Save decisions and paragraphs as you research. Your research trail is reconstructible, for colleagues and for the file.
